draft.title: Judging scientific evidence
card: data collected first-hand by the investigator, such as measuring the growth of bean plants in your own experiment.
data collected by someone else, such as figures from a published study or a government health report.
Good evidence is valid: the method tests what it claims to test. It is also authoritative: it comes from people with expertise, and it is often published and checked by other experts.
Good evidence is also checked for bias, such as a funder who gains from a certain result. An opinion or a personal story (an anecdote) is not good evidence, because it is not measured or tested.
draft.remember: Judge a source by its method, its author and its bias, not by how sure it sounds.

a.q: Which source is the best scientific evidence that a new fertiliser increases crop yield?
opts: A controlled trial published in a peer-reviewed journal
A farmer's story that her crops did well last year
A social media post praising the fertiliser
A company advertisement stating that yields doubled
a.why: A controlled trial that other experts have reviewed is valid and authoritative. The farmer's story is an anecdote, so it is not measured or tested, and it is the most tempting wrong option because it comes from real experience.
a.clue: Which source was tested and checked by experts?

b.q: Priya wants to know if sleep affects memory. She uses test scores that a university team collected and published. What kind of data is this, and what should she check?
opts: Secondary data, and whether the team had bias
Secondary data, and that she collected it herself
Primary data, and whether the team had bias
Primary data, and that she collected it herself
b.why: Priya did not collect the scores, so they are secondary data. Published data can still be affected by bias, such as a funder who gains from a result, so she should check for it. It is not primary data, because primary data is collected first-hand by the investigator.
b.clue: Who collected the data, and could that group gain from the result?

a.best: A controlled trial published in a peer-reviewed journal

b.best: Secondary data, and whether the team had bias
